{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"Every Thursday, someone left a single blue button on the bench outside the train station. They were never quite alike: one had four holes, another was shaped like a flower, and one still carried a loop of red thread.

Nico, who swept the platforms, kept them in a tin behind the ticket window. He told himself he was collecting litter, though he had never saved anything else he found.

In November, the buttons stopped appearing. Instead, a note lay on the bench: I’VE RUN OUT.

Nico read it twice. On his break, he dug through a drawer at home and found a brass button from a coat he no longer owned. He placed it on the bench before the first train arrived.

The next day, a woman in a green scarf stood beside it. She looked at the button but didn’t pick it up.

“My father used to sit here,” she said when Nico came to sweep. “He had a shop that repaired clothes. After he died, I found a jar of buttons under his counter. I thought leaving them might make someone wonder about him.”

“I did,” Nico said.

She smiled. “What was he like?”

Nico had never met the man, so he asked her instead. They sat through two departures while she told him about the shop, her father’s terrible singing, and the way he saved buttons because someone always needed one.

Before she left, Nico gave her the tin. She opened it and laughed softly at the little collection. Then she chose his brass button and pinned it to her scarf with a safety pin."}
